name: fix-agent-guide-drift-per-scope
body: source: requirements.requirement.agent-guide-drift-check said the self-test asserts "every token the implemented format defines appears in the relevant guide", listing among the tokens every `kalide.yaml` key and every CLI command (`init`, `init-library`, `start`, `templates`, `templates <name>`, `version`); inconsistency: the two guides have different declared scopes — requirements.requirement.library-agent-guide does not include the `kalide.yaml` config keys or the `init`/`version` CLI, so a literal reading of "the relevant guide" forced the library guide to duplicate the deck guide's config/CLI reference (feedback-4, NON-BLOCKING). resolution [with user, per reviewer suggestion]: redefined coverage per guide, keeping it mechanically checkable. (1) A union check: every format token (field types, reserved names `deck`/`slide` and `notes`/`body`/`_format`, the `media` helper, the reserved context keys, the `template.yaml` keys/body modes, the `library.yaml` keys) must appear in at least one guide; a token in neither guide fails. (2) Page scope checks: the deck guide (agent-authoring) must carry every `kalide.yaml` key and the full CLI command set; the library guide (library-agent-guide) must carry the library layout, the `library.yaml` keys, the `template.yaml` schema and body modes, the layout language/context/helper, every field type, and themes and media rules. (3) An explicit exclusion: the library guide's scope does NOT include the `kalide.yaml` keys or the `init`/`version` CLI, and the self-test must not require them there. The AC now distinguishes a guide-scoped removal (fails) from a shared token removed from both guides or a newly added token documented in neither (fails) from a token deliberately out of one guide's scope (does not fail). Only requirements.requirement.agent-guide-drift-check was amended; the declared scopes of agent-authoring and library-agent-guide are unchanged. [with user]
